sn12.39:1.2: “Bhikkhus, what one intends, and what one plans, and whatever one has a tendency towards: this becomes a basis for the maintenance of consciousness.
sn12.39:1.3: When there is a basis, there is a support for the establishing of consciousness.
sn12.39:1.4: When consciousness is established and has come to growth, there is a descent of name-and-form.
sn12.39:1.5: With name-and-form as condition, the six sense bases come to be;
sn12.39:1.6: with the six sense bases as condition, contact;
sn12.39:1.13: sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair come to be.
sn12.39:1.14: Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.
sn12.39:2.1: “If, bhikkhus, one does not intend, and one does not plan, but one still has a tendency towards something, this becomes a basis for the maintenance of consciousness.
sn12.39:2.2: When there is a basis, there is a support for the establishing of consciousness.
sn12.39:2.3: When consciousness is established and has come to growth, there is a descent of name-and-form.
sn12.39:2.4: With name-and-form as condition, the six sense bases come to be….
sn12.39:2.5: Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.
sn12.39:3.1: “But, bhikkhus, when one does not intend, and one does not plan, and one does not have a tendency towards anything, no basis exists for the maintenance of consciousness.
sn12.39:3.2: When there is no basis, there is no support for the establishing of consciousness.
sn12.39:3.3: When consciousness is unestablished and does not come to growth, there is no descent of name-and-form.
sn12.39:3.4: With the cessation of name-and-form comes cessation of the six sense bases….
sn12.39:3.5: Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”
